audit.why: Packet win rate 51.46% over 171 games matches MC_WR_TABLES.zac.ambessa = 51.46. No elo-tier language in either layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is built around an ability called 'Repeating Dashes'. Ambessa has no such ability. It appears in 25 separate writable strings — tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, loading, focus.text, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[5].why, six breakdown keys, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[2].d and seven report entries — and it is the ability the entire matchup tells the player to track.
audit.why: Ambessa's kit is Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E) and Public Execution (R). 'Repeating Dashes' is a description of what Drakehound's Step does, not a name Riot uses. The packet's suspectNames is empty for this matchup because the string is too far from any real name to register as a near miss, so the automated pass missed it entirely — it only flagged that no abilities are named. This is the same class of error as 'Ares of Blaze' for Brand's R in the calibration list, but larger: it is the single most repeated proper noun in the matchup. focus.text is literally 'Ambessa Repeating Dashes', so the loading screen shows the player a fabricated ability name.
audit.corrected: Replaced every occurrence with Public Execution. Two reasons over the alternatives. First, the surrounding framing is always 'track it, engage when it is down' — Drakehound's Step is a passive with no cooldown, so that sentence cannot be made true with it; Public Execution is 130/115/100s and is the cooldown that actually decides whether Zac may commit. Second, the content layer already independently identifies her R as the thing that beats Zac's health pool, so this makes the two layers agree. Public Execution is also exactly 16 characters, the same as the string it replaces, so every swap is length-neutral.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.focus is {text: 'Ambessa Repeating Dashes', letters: ['E']} — the fabricated name is paired with the E slot.
audit.why: The letters array suggests the generator meant Lacerate, Ambessa's E. But Lacerate is 13/12/11/10/9s and effectively always available, so 'engage only on its cooldown' is not actionable advice, whereas Public Execution at 130s at rank 1 is exactly the window Zac needs. I have set focus.text to Public Execution to match the rest of the repair.
audit.corrected: focus.letters must move from ['E'] to ['R'] alongside the focus.text edit. Not proposed as an edit because it is an array of tokens, not a string, and the applier's writable-path contract covers strings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Public Execution is described only as 'a hard-lockdown all-in' and 'lockdown all-in'. Neither layer says what the lockdown actually is, and neither mentions its targeting rule.
audit.why: Two things Riot states outright and the guide omits. First, it 'SUPPRESSES them upon her arrival' and then stuns — suppression is a distinct and much stronger category than a stun, and calling it generic lockdown hides that. Second, and decisively for a tank: she 'blinks to the FARTHEST enemy champion in a line of her choosing'. Zac's whole late-game job is standing in front of his carries, and this ability specifically ignores the person in front. A Zac player who does not know that will body-block for a backline that was never protected.
audit.corrected: Put the suppress-then-stun wording into content.mid, whys[4], spikes[1].text, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t, and the farthest-target rule into content.spikes[3].text and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Repudiation is never mentioned in either layer, and neither is the Cunning Sweep to Sundering Slam transformation.
audit.why: Repudiation 'gains a shield, briefly braces herself, and then slams the ground... If she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage.' That makes it an actively punishing ability to trade into, which matters enormously for Zac because Unstable Matter is a flat 5s pulse he will otherwise happily tick into her brace and pay for. On the Q side, 'Striking an enemy will transform the next cast of this ability' — Cunning Sweep becomes Sundering Slam, so the second Q in a sequence is a different, longer-ranged ability. The guide's repeated advice to 'dodge her Q edges' treats both casts as the same shape.
audit.corrected: Added the brace-punishes-damage rule to content.early and wants.you[0], and the Q transformation to spikes[0].text and whys[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Drakehound's Step is described only as 'her chained dashes' and 'dash mobility'.
audit.why: The actual rule is specific and worth knowing: 'Entering an attack or movement command while casting an ability will cause Ambessa to dash a short distance once the ability is cast.' The dash is not on its own cooldown — it rides every ability she casts, and it also grants her next attack bonus range and damage. That is why Elastic Slingshot's charge-up is so exploitable here, and it also means _missing-interactions' auto-reset warning is about the passive, not about a separate spell.
audit.corrected: Named Drakehound's Step and stated the rides-every-cast rule in content.early, whys[0], whys[1], spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0] and dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.breakdown.cooldowns names the fabricated ability and fills its other two bullets with unnamed placeholders — 'Your committal tool' and 'Your ultimate'. No number appears anywhere in it.
audit.why: The three numbers that decide this lane are Public Execution at 130s at rank 1, Lacerate at 13s, and Zac's Elastic Slingshot at 21s at rank 1. The gap between 130 and 13 is the whole point: one of her abilities is worth waiting out and the other never is, and the guide's blanket 'engage only on its cooldown' framing cannot distinguish them while the ability is fictional.
audit.corrected: Rebuilt the bullet list around those three real cooldowns.

notes: HIGHEST-PRIORITY ITEM IN THIS SLICE. 'Repeating Dashes' is a fabricated ability name occupying 25 writable strings in champ-data/zac.full.js for this matchup, including focus.text, which means the loading screen shows the player an ability Ambessa does not have. The automated pass could not catch it: suspectNames is empty because the string is too distant from any real Ambessa name to score as a near miss, and the only defect raised was the generic 'never names any of Ambessa's abilities'. That detection gap is worth acting on beyond this matchup — a name-invention check should test every capitalised multi-word noun phrase in a matchup against the enemy's kit ability list, not just fuzzy-match the ones that are already close. I have proposed length-neutral swaps for all 25 (Public Execution is exactly the same 16 characters as Repeating Dashes), but two things still need a human. First, full.focus.letters is ['E'] and must move to ['R'] to match focus.text; it is an array rather than a string so it is outside the edit contract. Second, I chose Public Execution over Drakehound's Step deliberately — the generator's letters array points at E, but every sentence around the name says 'track it, engage when it is down', which is meaningless for a passive and near-meaningless for a 13s ability, whereas her 130s ultimate is genuinely the window Zac waits for. If the user prefers fidelity to the original intent over usefulness, the alternative repair is Lacerate throughout, which breaks the length band on dosFull[0].t and focus.text and would need those two rewritten. Deliberately not asserted: whether Public Execution's suppression can be cleansed or QSS'd, and whether Repudiation's brace blocks or merely reduces incoming damage. ambessa.json needsResearch is empty and the brief forbids inferring either from the file.
